senses.definition: A set that holds everything another set holds, and more besides.
senses.caution: It is a precise claim and people check it. Ninety percent of the old thing plus some new things is not a superset, and the missing ten percent is exactly what the objection will be about — so either defend nothing is lost or say covers most of. Used loosely about a person's skills or a team's remit it stops being maths and starts sounding like a ranking.
senses.example: The new API is a strict superset of the old one, so nothing anybody has built stops working.

cues.text: You are reassuring a team that the replacement platform does everything the old one did and more, so nothing they rely on disappears.
A sponsor asks whether consolidating three tools into one will cost anybody a capability they currently have.
In an architecture review you want the exact word for a new interface that contains every method of the previous one.
You are pushing back on a migration plan because the target covers only most of what the current system does, not all of it.

distractors: A slice of the market defined by the industry it serves, such as banking or health.
An isolated environment where something runs without touching anything real.
A rule of thumb that gets you a good enough answer quickly.
To make a bad situation worse.
Alert and responsive to signals, adjusting early.
